answered_items.settled_by: **Yes - and structurally, not by luck.** The ID is a function of the message text, carried in the message's type, which both compilers spell the same way. All nine catalogs on disk are byte-identical. The *release-to-release* instability is a separate defect - **DEF-6**

answered_items.section_title: The items that are answered or contingent
answered_items.settled_by: **No, and it never did.** `<true>` means *"honour the per-logger immediate-flush threshold"*, and the check returns immediately when the threshold is 0. The threshold **is** 0 - it defaults to 0 and the project never calls `set_immediate_flush()`. Quill's own default is the same value, so the module path already matches quill's macro-free default

answered_items.section_title: The items that are answered or contingent
answered_items.settled_by: **Not a measurement.** The project has no `.github/` directory and no git remote, so the coverage gate, the format check and the clang-tidy check have no home until CI exists. `BUILD-5` ("should there be CI?") is an owner decision and is still open; this question is answered by it, not by a run
answered_items.title: What CI image would provide `gcov-16`?

answered_items.section_title: The items that are answered or contingent
answered_items.settled_by: **No.** At the pinned baseline the upstream `quill` port has **no `features` key at all** and depends only on `vcpkg-cmake` and `vcpkg-cmake-config`; its portfile passes no fmt option. quill 13.1.0's own CMakeLists has no fmt switch either - none of its 26 `option()` calls mentions fmt - and it installs `include/quill/bundled/fmt/*` unconditionally, exposing it as the `fmtquill` interface target. So **the two copies of fmt are structural**
answered_items.title: Does the upstream vcpkg `quill` port have an opt-in feature for an external fmt?

answered_items.section_title: The items that are answered or contingent
answered_items.settled_by: **No.** The baseline's tree was enumerated in full (17,869 paths, not truncated): none of `ut`, `intel-cib`, `intel-cpp-std-extensions`, `intel-baremetal-concurrency` or `intel-baremetal-senders-and-receivers` appears in `ports/` or in `versions/`. So all five **track upstream rather than the pinned baseline**
